abstract: Loss-of-function (LoF) mutations of the SCN2A gene, coding for Nav1.2 Na+ channels, are among the leading genetic contributors to autism spectrum disorders and intellectual disability (ASD/ID). The haploinsufficient Scn2a knock-out mouse (Scn2a+/-), displaying ASD/ID-like phenotypes, is commonly used as model for this channelopathy, although this specific mutation has not been identified in patients. We investigated the action potential (AP) generation in the axon initial segment (AIS) of layer-5 neocortical pyramidal neurons in wild-type (Scn2a+/+) mice, in Scn2a+/- mice and in mice carrying the missense mutation L1314P (Scn2a+/L1314P), identified in an ASD/ID patient. We recorded somatic action potentials (APs), and imaged Na+, Ca2+ and APs in the AIS, in females during postnatal (P) P21-40. During maturation from P21-24 to P30-40: (1) the ratio between Na+ influx in proximal and distal AIS sites (Rp/d) increased; (2) the delay between distal and proximal Ca2+ currents increased; (3) the half-width of the AP (APwid) in the soma decreased. We revealed that this maturation process is different in both Scn2a+/- and Scn2a+/L1314P mice, but in divergent manner. With respect to Scn2a+/+, Scn2a+/- cells were characterised by smaller Rp/d and delay values at P30-40, and wider somatic APwid at P21-24, whereas Scn2a+/L1314P cells by shorter AIS APwid at P21-24. Using a biophysical model, mimicking maturation changes in terms of Nav1.2, of a K+ channel and of voltage-gated Ca2+ channels, we reproduced the ensemble of experimental results, establishing that Scn2a+/- cells exhibit a combination of Nav1.2 LoF and delayed development, whereas Scn2a+/L1314P cells are characterised by AIS disruption involving strongly increased functional K+ channels. We conclude that diverse Nav1.2 LoF cases lead to different developmental paths involving other channels.
